# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. The one exception is if you need to run a fridge, cooler, or heavier gear for several days.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249) is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb, but only 300W of AC output. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mostly available through Amazon and other retailers. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299) has 286Wh and a 600W inverter, and can expand to 572Wh. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199) has 288Wh, a built-in lantern, and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" version. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179) is the budget pick, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Mid-size: a 12V fridge, power tools, or small kitchen appliances
- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh of LiFePO4, an 1,800W inverter, and a 5-year warranty, and weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). It lists at $499, and the code AFF5OFF reportedly brings it to $474.05. It has no expansion port. [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link; the site says it earns a commission at no cost to you; [details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)). Check the final price at checkout.

## Multi-day off-grid camping
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping (score 81). It has 2,042Wh, 2,200W output, and weighs 39 lb. List price is $1,499, but it was reported under $900 on sale. It can't run a space heater or an electric burner for long. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's best for camping. It has 1,536Wh, is IP65-rated, and weighs just under 40 lb. It was listed at $1,079-$1,199. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799) is the step-up pick for van life or a 12V fridge, and TechRadar also picked it for camping. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Things to know
- The reviewers don't fully agree. OutdoorGearLab scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker Solix C300 (50) fairly low in its lab tests, and favored larger units. Its value pick is the **Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2** (list $799, reportedly under $530 on sale). [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier to stretch battery life, since it can triple the draw. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- Prices change, and Black Friday sales are coming in November, so it may be worth waiting. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- Other than the Bluetti AC180, I only have review-page links with retailer buttons, not direct product links. Check the current price and model on the retailer's page before you buy.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow this to one pick.
